clue.text: Southern headland with river cutting through tight spot

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south or southern

indicators.note: the river slices into the headland, so its letter sits inside that word

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A geographical description of a promontory in the south with a river slicing across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting through' puts R inside CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, a synonym for a tight spot or fix.

clue.text: Break in journey provost arranged when going round Orient?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the eastern letter
the letters of the official's title are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Orient is the East, giving E

explanation.surface: A college provost organising a stop on a trip to the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes STOPOVR from PROVOST, and 'going round' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a brief stay partway through a longer trip, a break in travel.

clue.text: Pass on Marmite mother's left for spreading

indicators.note: the remaining letters are spread about into a new order
the mother has gone, so her letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written; a British yeast-extract spread
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother has left the Marmite out for spreading on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British yeast spread. 'left' removes MA, leaving RMITE, which 'for spreading' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to pass on or refer, as a matter remitted to another court.

clue.text: Creature beginning to pollen part of flower

indicators.note: the start of the next word is taken

parts.note: an anther is the pollen-bearing part of a flower's stamen

explanation.surface: Botany: pollen beginning to form in part of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a wild creature.

clue.text: Factory in which one must be seen as flexible

indicators.note: says the factory word holds the single letter for one inside it

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A factory that needs to be adaptable, as if a works must be seen to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts I inside PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant is a direct synonym of flexible, describing something that bends easily or yields.

clue.text: Person receiving money of late

parts.note: of late seems to mean recently, but it means from the late, a deceased person who left money

explanation.surface: Someone who has been getting money recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of late' looks like 'recently' but means from someone deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a beneficiary named in a will, receiving a bequest from the dead.

clue.text: A wretched cold

parts.note: pathetic means wretched or pitiful

explanation.surface: Complaining of a miserable cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like the illness but is the definition: emotionally unmoved.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no feeling or interest, which is a cold, indifferent attitude.

clue.text: Resident football team missing one six-footer

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, so one fewer leaves ten
an ant is an insect, which has six legs

explanation.surface: A local footballer, one short of a full side, standing over six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect, with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is someone who occupies a property, a resident.

clue.text: Where numbers can be found all day and all night

definitions.meaning: the numerals of a clock face are positioned on a circle around it
continuously, without stopping for twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: Searching for figures at every hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Round-the-clock describes nonstop activity, and literally the dial's circumference is where the hours sit.

clue.text: Order duck for serviceman

parts.note: a command is an order
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so it gives the letter O for zero

explanation.surface: An instruction to a duck, perhaps by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a member of an elite military unit, a kind of serviceman.

clue.text: Relative managed to find accommodation in grand US city

indicators.note: the managing word is lodged within the other letters, as a guest is accommodated

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand
NY is short for New York
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A relative who managed to find lodgings in a big American city.
explanation.walkthrough: G is slang for a grand (a thousand pounds or dollars).
explanation.definitionFit: A granny is a grandmother, a family relative.

clue.text: Office mailbag

definitions.meaning: a position or job held, as in a government appointment
letters and parcels delivered, the contents of a mailbag

explanation.surface: A workplace sack of letters, as in a postroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a job or office held, and the post is the mail collected and delivered.

clue.text: At close quarters to workers on both sides

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
the same workers word used again for the other side

explanation.surface: Instructions for labour placed on either side of something, close together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on both sides' means a HAND goes on each side of TO, so the workers word is used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-to-hand combat is fighting at very close range, in physical contact.

clue.text: Attend a sanctuary and go into withdrawal

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
a retreat is a quiet refuge or sanctuary

explanation.surface: Going to a spiritual retreat to withdraw from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attend' is read as BE AT, which run together with A and RETREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a retreat is to withdraw hastily, especially of an army falling back.

clue.text: Time to appear in strange tableau daughter carefully organised

indicators.note: the time letter shows up within the rearranged letters
something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter carefully setting up an odd living tableau, timed to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' makes TABULAE from TABLEAU and 'to appear in' puts T inside it, before D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabulated data is arranged systematically in a table, carefully set out.

clue.text: What those with largest families do last of all

definitions.text: What those with largest families do
definitions.meaning: parents of the biggest families bring up, or rear, the greatest number of children
positioned furthest back, at the very end

explanation.surface: A remark about big families and what they do in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means furthest to the back, and read as two words it is raising the greatest number of children.

clue.text: Glassy-eyed, quite a sight in bed

indicators.note: the sight is placed inside the bed word

parts.note: taken as written
a spectacle is quite a sight, a striking display

explanation.surface: Someone dazed and staring, making an exhibition of themselves in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glassy-eyed' usually means vacant, but here it means wearing glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bespectacled wears glasses, so is jokingly glassy-eyed.

clue.text: Lean left in poster?

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the poster word

parts.note: one who posts a letter is a sender

explanation.surface: A thin figure on the left of a wall poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' looks like a placard but is someone who posts mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means thin or slim, a synonym of lean as an adjective.

clue.text: Old tape repaired jumper at an earlier stage

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Mending an old woolly jumper with tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater but is a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog, which jumps, begins life as a tadpole, its larval stage.

clue.text: Don't get the wind up

parts.note: the idiom means keep from panicking, but it also describes a sailing ship left without any breeze

explanation.surface: Reassurance not to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as BE CALM, an instruction not to panic; whole, a ship that is becalmed gets no wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Becalm means to leave a sailing vessel motionless for lack of breeze, and be calm means stay composed.

clue.text: Rich source listed

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a ship that has heeled has listed or leaned over to one side

explanation.surface: A wealthy origin appearing on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listed' is the nautical sense: leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an informal idiom for wealthy or prosperous.

clue.text: Change lines to be delivered by Virginia

indicators.note: the lines come after Virginia, as if handed on from that state

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A US state sending lines that bring change, perhaps a script being delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' is railway lines, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or modify, a verb synonym of change.

clue.text: Minister making some civic arrangements

indicators.note: making some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clergyman taking part in organising town affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, a minister of the Church of England.

clue.text: Ate sandwiches a good person went without

indicators.note: the eating word encloses the other letters like bread round a filling

parts.note: fed means ate, as in the animals fed
ST is short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Someone ate sandwiches while a virtuous person went hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fasted is to have gone without food deliberately.

clue.text: Hurry up with double portion of food

indicators.note: signals that the portion word is given two times over

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat, a portion of food

explanation.surface: An impatient diner wanting a quick double helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exclamation urging someone to be quick.

clue.text: New style our ships must follow

indicators.note: the ships come after the style word

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's ships

explanation.surface: A new design that British ships must adopt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our' is the British setter's view, so the ships are the Royal Navy (RN).
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, a synonym of new.

clue.text: Seek measures with rights enshrined

indicators.note: the rights are held inside the measures, as in a shrine

parts.note: feet are units of length, measures
R stands for right, so two rights give RR

explanation.surface: Seeking legal measures that protect rights.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret, or ferret out, is to search persistently, like the animal hunting rabbits.
